doc.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Commissions in Europe
summary: Commissions such as the Slovenian symphony and Denmark came from working abroad with radio bands.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Oh man, to this day, certain orchestras I love writing for that I would do even though I know they can’t always afford to pay my price. But I mean you figure my God. It opens up other doors too. It all depends, especially now we’re getting a lot of composing commissions. Many composing commissions. Not only for band but orchestral, for big bands. Now that’s important. You’re getting your music out there and you’re getting into another trend. Now a lot of these bands are for a symphony in Slovenia believe it or not. I was over there last year with the radio band which is very good. Now I’m being

commissioned by the symphony to write a piece for the Slovenian Symphony and the big band. So being over there for one thing, letting them be aware that I was doing this sort of stuff, now the same thing almost in Denmark is happening. So I mean there’s a lot of things that you can’t — I can’t remember the saying — but there’s, you know you don’t look at the moment you’ve got to look at where this thing is going. You know, where this project is going. It’s an ego trip too, you say wow, I’m going to have all these guys playing my music and this audience listening to it. And it opens other doors for you.
